items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: He hired Sonny, himself on guitar, Chris Henderson on piano, Wilbur Campbell on drums. ... Okay, a gig is a gig. I think we made $10 a night. ... We'd go over there, and oh, we thought we were playing some blues.

ctx.x: I got to tell you this, though ... this happened, I think before Sonny Rollins -- this happened in '55, after I left Griffin. The little guitar player I was raised up with out in Chicago, Leo Blevins, a little short dude -- he would come and stay right on top of everybody that played. And he didn't fool around or nothing like that, but he was in your corner, and he knew who to get -- he could play himself; he had a brother played piano named Bobby -- but Leo come and

got Sonny Rollins, who was out there then -- that's where he joined Max to return back east, and he says, "I got a gig." He hired Sonny, himself on guitar, Chris Henderson on piano, Wilbur Campbell on drums. He said, "Man, we got to go on the West Side and play this gig." And he would say, "We got to play blues now." And that means fast blues, slow blues, shuffle blues -- that's all they want to hear.

Okay, a gig is a gig. I think we made $10 a night. But it was worth it. We'd go over there, and oh, we thought we were playing some blues. We got funky -- Leo even fell on his knees; he could do that ... fell on his knees bending them strings, you know; something like T-Bone Walker would do, and when we finished playing the blues, we thought we really had gotten to the people, and some guy way in the back of the club hollered, "All right now, why don't you play some blues!" And he had taken all of the starch out…
